Work over \(\mathbb C\). A rank-\(r\) algebraic vector bundle \(E\) on \(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\) is called uniform if there are integers \(a_1\ge\cdots\ge a_r\) such that, for every projective line \(L\subset\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\),
\[
E|_L\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathcal O_L(a_i),
\]
where \(\mathcal O_L(a)\) denotes the line bundle of degree \(a\) on \(L\cong\mathbb P^1\). Call \(E\) homogeneous if \(g^*E\cong E\) for every projective linear automorphism \(g\in\operatorname{PGL}_{n+1}(\mathbb C)\).

\[
d=\min\left\{n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}:\text{there exists a uniform, non-homogeneous algebraic vector bundle on }\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\text{ of some rank }1\le r<2n\right\},
\]
with the convention \(\min\varnothing=+\infty\).
</problem>

43	## 2. A rank-nine bundle on \(\mathbb P^5\)

46	\[
47	0\longrightarrow\mathcal O(-1)
48	 \longrightarrow V\otimes\mathcal O
49	 \longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow0
50	\]
51	for the tautological sequence. Thus \(Q=T_{\mathbb P^5}(-1)\) has rank \(5\).
52	
53	Set
54	\[
55	F=\Lambda^2Q,
56	\qquad \operatorname{rank}F=10.
57	\]
58	Choose a basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_5\) of \(V\), and the nondegenerate bivector
59	\[
60	\omega=e_0\wedge e_1+e_2\wedge e_3+e_4\wedge e_5.
61	\]
62	Its image in \(H^0(F)\) defines a section \(s_\omega\). Define \(E_\omega\) by
63	\[
64	0\longrightarrow\mathcal O
65	 \xrightarrow{s_\omega}F
66	 \longrightarrow E_\omega\longrightarrow0.                 \tag{1}
67	\]
68	
69	First, \(s_\omega\) is nowhere zero. At \(x=[\ell]\in\mathbb P(V)\), its value is the image of \(\omega\) in
70	\[
71	\Lambda^2(V/\ell).
72	\]
73	If this image were zero, then \(\omega\in\ell\wedge V\). But every bivector in \(\ell\wedge V\) has rank at most \(2\), whereas \(\omega\) has rank \(6\).
74	
75	Therefore \(E_\omega\) is an algebraic vector bundle of rank
76	\[
77	10-1=9<10=2\cdot5.
78	\]
79	
80	## 3. Uniformity
81	
82	Let \(L=\mathbb P(W)\), where \(W\subset V\) has dimension \(2\). On \(L\),
83	\[
84	Q|_L\cong\mathcal O_L(1)\oplus\mathcal O_L^{\,4},
85	\]
86	so
87	\[
88	F|_L\cong\mathcal O_L(1)^{\,4}\oplus\mathcal O_L^{\,6}.       \tag{2}
89	\]
90	
91	The component of \(s_\omega|_L\) in the trivial quotient in (2) is precisely the image of \(\omega\) in
92	\[
93	\Lambda^2(V/W).
94	\]
95	It is nonzero. Indeed, otherwise
96	\[
97	\omega\in W\wedge V.
98	\]
99	Relative to a decomposition \(V=W\oplus U\), a bivector in \(W\wedge V\) has skew matrix
100	\[
101	\begin{pmatrix}
102	 A&B\\
103	 -B^{\mathsf T}&0
104	\end{pmatrix},
105	\qquad \dim W=2,
106	\]
107	whose rank is at most \(4\). This contradicts \(\operatorname{rank}\omega=6\).
108	
109	Thus the section in (2) has a nonzero constant component. An automorphism of the bundle in (2) takes it to one of the trivial summands: first change basis among the trivial summands, and then subtract its \(\mathcal O(1)\)-components.
110	
111	Taking the quotient gives, for **every** line \(L\),
112	\[
113	E_\omega|_L
114	 \cong\mathcal O_L(1)^{\,4}\oplus\mathcal O_L^{\,5}.          \tag{3}
115	\]
116	Hence \(E_\omega\) is uniform.
117	
118	## 4. Non-homogeneity
119	
120	We prove something stronger: the isomorphism class of \(E_\omega\), as a bundle over the fixed projective space, determines the projective parameter \([\omega]\).
121	
122	### 4.1 Two cohomology calculations
123	
124	We need
125	\[
126	H^0(F)=\Lambda^2V,\qquad
127	H^0(F^*)=H^1(F^*)=0.                                     \tag{4}
128	\]
129	
130	For the first assertion, the exterior tautological sequence is
131	\[
132	0\longrightarrow Q(-1)
133	 \longrightarrow\Lambda^2V\otimes\mathcal O
134	 \longrightarrow F\longrightarrow0.
135	\]
136	The sequence
137	\[
138	0\longrightarrow\mathcal O(-2)
139	 \longrightarrow V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)
140	 \longrightarrow Q(-1)\longrightarrow0
141	\]
142	shows that \(Q(-1)\) is acyclic on \(\mathbb P^5\). This proves the first assertion.
143	
144	For the second, \(F^*=\Omega^2(2)\), and the exterior Euler complex is
145	\[
146	0\longrightarrow F^*
147	 \longrightarrow\Lambda^2V^*\otimes\mathcal O
148	 \longrightarrow V^*\otimes\mathcal O(1)
149	 \longrightarrow\mathcal O(2)\longrightarrow0.
150	\]
151	Its complex of global sections is
152	\[
153	0\longrightarrow\Lambda^2V^*
154	 \longrightarrow V^*\otimes V^*
155	 \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^2V^*
156	 \longrightarrow0,
157	\]
158	which is exact. Since the displayed line bundles have no higher cohomology, this gives the required vanishings.
159	
160	### 4.2 The bundle \(F\) is simple
161	
162	We claim
163	\[
164	\operatorname{End}(F)=\mathbb C.                            \tag{5}
165	\]
166	
167	An endomorphism of the globally generated bundle \(F\) induces an endomorphism
168	\[
169	A:\Lambda^2V\longrightarrow\Lambda^2V.
170	\]
171	At \(x=[\ell]\), the evaluation kernel is \(\ell\wedge V\). Hence \(A\) preserves \(\ell\wedge V\) for every \(\ell\).
172	
173	For independent \(x,y\in V\),
174	\[
175	(x\wedge V)\cap(y\wedge V)=\mathbb C(x\wedge y).
176	\]
177	Thus every decomposable bivector is an eigenvector of \(A\). In particular,
178	\[
179	A(e_i\wedge e_j)=\lambda_{ij}e_i\wedge e_j.
180	\]
181	Applying the same assertion to \((e_i+e_k)\wedge e_j\) gives
182	\[
183	\lambda_{ij}=\lambda_{kj}
184	\]
185	for distinct indices. All the \(\lambda_{ij}\) are therefore equal. Since evaluation is surjective, \(A\), and hence the original bundle endomorphism, is scalar. This proves (5).
186	
187	### 4.3 Recovering the defining section
188	
189	Dualizing (1) and using (4) gives
190	\[
191	H^1(E_\omega^*)\cong\mathbb C.
192	\]
193	Equivalently,
194	\[
195	\operatorname{Ext}^1(E_\omega,\mathcal O)\cong\mathbb C.     \tag{6}
196	\]
197	Sequence (1) is nonsplit: a splitting would give a nonzero map \(F\to\mathcal O\), contradicting \(H^0(F^*)=0\).
198	
199	Suppose now that \(\omega,\eta\) are nondegenerate and
200	\[
201	E_\omega\cong E_\eta.
202	\]
203	By (6), their nonsplit extensions by \(\mathcal O\) are identified up to a nonzero scalar on \(\mathcal O\). This produces an automorphism of their middle term \(F\) carrying the line spanned by \(s_\omega\) to that spanned by \(s_\eta\).
204	
205	By (5), that automorphism is scalar. Using \(H^0(F)=\Lambda^2V\), we obtain
206	\[
207	E_\omega\cong E_\eta
208	\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
209	[\omega]=[\eta]\text{ in }\mathbb P(\Lambda^2V).            \tag{7}
210	\]
211	
212	### 4.4 A projective automorphism changes the isomorphism class
213	
214	Take
215	\[
216	G=\operatorname{diag}(2,1,1,1,1,1).
217	\]
218	Then
219	\[
220	(\Lambda^2G)\omega
221	 =2e_0\wedge e_1+e_2\wedge e_3+e_4\wedge e_5
222	\]
223	is not proportional to \(\omega\).
224	
225	For the projective automorphism induced by \(G^{-1}\), the natural identification of the pulled-back tautological sequence with the original one gives
226	\[
227	g^*E_\omega\cong E_{(\Lambda^2G)\omega}.
228	\]
229	By (7), this is not isomorphic to \(E_\omega\). Therefore \(E_\omega\) is **not homogeneous**.
230	
231	Together with (3), this proves \(d\leq5\), completing the mathematical argument.
232	
233	## 5. Exact Python checks
234	
235	The following code uses exact symbolic arithmetic. In particular, the rank obstruction used for **all** lines is checked by identically vanishing symbolic minors, not random samples.
236

305	def h_line(n, t, q):
306	    if q == 0 and t >= 0:

317	# Preservation of all e_i wedge V kills every off-diagonal entry.
318	allowed = []

329	        if k in (i, j):
